newsitem.title: INDONESIA: FOCUS-Indonesian rupiah plunges, stocks volatile.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Indonesian rupiah plunges, stocks volatile.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah plunged on Tuesday along with the Malaysian ringgit and the Singapore dollar, triggering volatile trading on the battered stock market, brokers and dealers said.
The Indonesia stock market fell 1.36 percent in early trade, but shrugged off the losses to end up 0.73 percent at 662.95 points, the first time it closed higher since August 1.
Brokers said a wave of buying in PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom), the most heavily-weighted stock on the index, enlivened sentiment in the afternoon and propped up the market by the close.
Telkom closed up 125 rupiah at 3,800 after falling to a low of 3,550.
The head of research for a foreign brokerage said the fall in Telkom over the past week was overdone. "It's just a case of coming back up slightly," he said.
But he said the tone of the market was weak.
"People are still very nervous and will stay so until they see some stability on the currency front," he said.

"Initially, we thought that the Thai reforms package would help. But people are looking at the ability of the Thais to implement that package. There is instability there. Everything is very much up in the air."
An analyst at another foreign brokerage said it would take at least a month for the Jakarta stock market to stabilise.

"Today's rise was just a little bit of a bounce after six days of the market coming down," he said. "But there are currency problems and general volatility...it will take a while before it settles down."

The rupiah plunged some 30 points to 2,655 against the dollar in the morning after the Singapore dollar fell through a key support level of 1.50 to the U.S. unit and the Malaysian ringgit plunged to a 42-month low.
The rupiah had stabilised at 2,640.42 at the close of Jakarta trading but dealers said sentiment was poor.

"It's dangerous to take on heavy positions," said a Japanese bank dealer. "We don't know what the equilibrium level is now although some suggest the rupiah is undervalued. We just go with the market and regional trends."
The Singapore-based I.D.E.A. consultancy said the rupiah was still vulnerable to developments in Malaysia and Singapore.
"We may see 2,650/55 being tested again," it said in a report.
